summary: Mount Martha fire tower, Cherry Mountain, NH: built 1939; sources disagree on its end date (1968, 1982, 1989); footings remain on the summit.

facts.status_note: Only the footings remain on Mount Martha, per ScenicNH and a hiking article.

access.note: Reached on hiking trails; Mount Martha is on the 52 with a View hiking list.

visit.trail_note: Hike to Mount Martha; the old footings are on the summit.

events.note: A 1939 newspaper notice listed a tower as planned for Cherry Mountain; FFLA-cited dates in ScenicNH and a hiking article give construction in 1939
Razed, per a hiking article that credits FireLookout.org; not confirmed elsewhere
Dismantled, per FFLA-cited dates in ScenicNH and a hiking article

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not resolved. ScenicNH gives a 1939 to 1968 span but also cites FFLA for a 1989 dismantling. The hiking article gives razing in 1982 and dismantling in 1989. The story reports the 1939 build and the 1989 dismantling date that both posts attribute to FFLA, and flags the 1968 and 1982 dates as disagreements.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on end dates: ScenicNH's 1968 span, the hiking article's 1982 razing, and the 1989 dismantling that both cite to FFLA. The FFLA's own Cherry page returned 404 on fetch, so the FFLA dates are second-hand. The weirs article puts the mountain in 'Carrol/Twin Mountain' while the record and FFLA say Coos County; the story keeps Coos. The 1939 notice spells the name 'Charry' and gives 3,600 feet; Mount Martha is 3,573 feet per the hiking article. Staffing, fires and the wartime history are not in any fetched source and are left out. The 1980s demolition attempt appears only in ScenicNH; the 1982 razing appears only in the hiking article; they may describe the same event.
